summary:
IMPORTANT INFRASTRUCTURE BUG FOUND FIRST: the prompt I was given never actually contained the tickets -- benchmarks/fresh_ab/scale_authoring_wf.js line 500 has a double-templating bug (`${'${JSON.stringify(tickets, null, 1)}'}` emits the literal template string instead of interpolating the real `tickets` variable), so the live 'Verify' phase of this workflow never receives real ticket data through the prompt. I recovered the actual 20 authored tickets (DJ1-4, CE1-4, SA1-4, FL1-4, XL1-4) directly from the completed Author-phase job transcripts in ~/.claude/projects/.../subagents/workflows/wf_01e039a0-44e/agent-*.jsonl and verified those against django/celery/sqlalchemy/flask source. This templating bug should be fixed (drop the stray `${'...'}` wrapper around JSON.stringify(tickets,...) at line 500) before this workflow is trusted to self-verify in future runs.

Verification of the 20 recovered tickets: this is an unusually high-quality batch. All 20 pass on gold accuracy, primary_paths existence, and caller-set correctness -- I independently re-derived every blast-radius caller_set by grepping the target name and reading every hit, and found zero missed call sites and zero spurious call sites across all 16 single-repo tickets. All 4 cross-repo (XL) tickets' technical claims (class names, line numbers, mechanism descriptions) were verified against current source and are accurate, with one trivial imprecision in XL1 (a nested-function attribution) that does not affect its markers or correctness.

Two tickets (DJ2, DJ3) need a small repair: they carry gold_markers that are dangerously generic bare words -- 'login_required' (91 repo-wide hits) and 'permission_required' (62 hits) in DJ2, and 'QuerySet' (1062 hits) in DJ3 -- which would silently credit an arm for incidental, unrelated mentions rather than for actually finding the real call sites. Fix: drop those specific markers, keep the rest (each ticket has several precise markers already).

Four tickets (CE3, SA3, SA4, FL4) carry unusable_reason because their genuinely correct answer is an empty or single-shared caller_set (Autoscale.convert only reached via click's polymorphic dispatch; MapperEvents._accept_with only reached via a runtime event-registry lookup; Result.partitions has zero internal callers; the 'wrapper' closures are never called by that name outside their own defining scope). I independently verified all four claims are accurate. I disagree with dropping them: each is a legitimate, well-supported hard case rather than a broken ticket, and together they give a reasonable difficulty spread (4 of 8 ambiguous single-repo tickets have real non-empty caller sets, the other 4 have correctly-empty ones). My recommendation is to keep all four, but the judging protocol must explicitly instruct graders to accept a well-explained 'no traceable in-repo call sites' answer as fully correct rather than penalizing an arm that (correctly) finds nothing.

Net result: 18/20 pass as-is, 2/20 (DJ2, DJ3) need a one-line marker-list edit before use -- no ticket needs to be rejected or rewritten.
